      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_uart",

    {
      "Candidate Name": "Hardware flow-control enable setting",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_uart",

    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Interrupt threshold enable settings",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_uart",
      "Merged Into": "C5",

    },

      "Candidate Name": "FIFO clear commands",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_uart",
      "Merged Into": "",

    {
      "Candidate Name": "FIFO occupancy and capacity flags",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_uart",

      "Candidate Name": "Serial synchronizer state",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_uart",

      "Why Not Kept": "rx_engine.sync only resamples uart_rxd_i before receive processing, so Working values and synchronizer-stage rules fold it into received data rather than making it a separate piece."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus access command",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_uart",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The bus request strobe, direction and address fields are access command fields for the unit's registers and FIFOs, which the access-command-fields rule excludes as concepts of their own."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus response acknowledge and constant error status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_uart",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The acknowledge only repeats the request strobe and the error field is tied to a constant, so Bus handshake copies excludes both as independent information."

      "Candidate Name": "UART clock source and internal timing pulse",

      "Merged Into": "C4",
      "Why Not Kept": "clkgen_i and uart_clk are clock or timing elements, and the clocks rule excludes the clock itself while the timing setting remains part of the baud and timing configuration."

      "Merged Into": "C1",
      "Why Not Kept": "The FIFO data signals only carry payload between the bus or receiver and the FIFO instances, so Port buffers treats them as copies while the transmitted and received data are judged at their unit boundaries."
    }

conceptual assets.information: Payload bytes accepted from the bus and transmitted on the UART output; normal transmit operation depends on preserving and forwarding these bytes. The payload enters through the bus and leaves through the UART output or the simulation logging path.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because bus payload data is exposed on uart_txd_o at line 392 and can also be written to the screen and simulation file at lines 499-511; integrity is at risk because the payload is loaded into the transmit FIFO at line 260 and into the transmit shift register at line 351, where unauthorized alteration changes the transmitted byte; availability is at risk because enable, simulation mode or the transmit-clear condition can clear the FIFO at line 259 and CTS can hold transmission in the wait state at lines 358-360; undermined expected behavior is possible because the simulation/test path clears normal transmit buffering and diverts payload bytes to logging at lines 259 and 499-511.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write or alter transmit data, enable simulation mode, clear the transmit FIFO, or hold CTS so that confidential bytes are exposed, corrupted, or never transmitted.

conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt or clear received bytes, or disable the receive path, causing software to read false data or lose incoming UART traffic.

conceptual assets.information: The operational enable setting that determines whether the UART engines, clock-enable output, interrupts and FIFOs are active. UART operation and preservation of buffered traffic depend on this state.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a bus write changes the stored enable state at line 179; availability is at risk because the state drives clkgen_en_o at line 228, controls both engines at lines 344 and 417, and can clear both FIFOs at lines 259 and 304.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write the control register to disable the UART, stop its clock generation, and clear pending transmit or receive data.

conceptual assets.information: The programmable prescaler and baud divisor that determine UART sampling and transmission timing. Correct timing is required for the UART to communicate reliably with its peer.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus writes change ctrl.prsc and ctrl.baud at lines 182-183; availability is at risk because these settings control uart_clk selection and baud counters at lines 229, 349, 368, 422 and 432, so unauthorized changes can make communication unusable.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the prescaler or baud divisor so that transmitted and received bits no longer match the peer's timing.

conceptual assets.information: The receive interrupt event indicating that receive FIFO occupancy has reached a configured condition. System software may depend on it to service received data before the FIFO overruns.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the receive interrupt output is generated from enable, interrupt settings and FIFO status at lines 315-318; availability is at risk because suppressing irq_rx_o can prevent software from servicing the receive FIFO and can contribute to lost data.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress or spuriously assert irq_rx_o so that software fails to service received data or services the FIFO at the wrong time.

conceptual assets.information: The transmit interrupt event indicating that the transmit FIFO has reached a configured empty or low-occupancy condition. System software may depend on it to provide more transmit data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because irq_tx_o is generated from enable, interrupt settings and transmit FIFO status at lines 270-272; availability is at risk because suppressing irq_tx_o can prevent software from replenishing the transmit FIFO and stall output.

conceptual assets.information: The RTS handshake indication that tells the UART peer whether this unit can accept more receive data. Its correct value is needed to prevent peer-side transmission from being blocked or overflowing the receive path.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the unit assigns uart_rtsn_o from enable, hardware-flow-control mode and receive FIFO occupancy at lines 472-480; availability is at risk because asserting uart_rtsn_o can withhold all peer transfers at line 475, while deasserting it when the FIFO is near full can cause receive loss.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the RTS indication to the blocking or non-blocking value, either stopping peer traffic or allowing traffic when the receive buffer cannot safely accept it.

conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could hold uart_ctsn_i in its blocking state or corrupt its sampled value so that the transmitter remains stalled.
